Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

pThroughput measured on the fourteen scratch hours (all coins, 402,328,613
bytes of lz4, one input set for every row; an earlier revision mixed a
ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

bytes of lz4, one input set for every row; an earlier revision mixed a
ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |

| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |

| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.

hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

ten-hour byte total into twelve-hour rows, which the review caught):

| jobs | threads/worker | wall | MB/s of lz4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 194.1 s | 2.1 |
| 4 | 4 | 72.9 s | 5.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 73.3 s | 5.5 |
| 16 | 4 | 86.8 s | 4.6 |
| 10 | 1 | 39.8 s | 10.1 |
| 12 | 1 | 28.6 s | 14.1 |

Measured on the shared box while the downloader itself was running (load
about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

about 20 of 128 cores). Downloads arrive at about 73 GB/h (20 MB/s), which
is the bar, and this box was short of it: 14.1 MB/s at the best setting.
The bottleneck is the serial per-hour work, not the job count. One all-coin
hour (20251001/0, 32.4 MB of lz4) takes 20.8 s with one DuckDB thread and
16.0 s with four, so roughly 13-15 s of each hour is single-threaded Rust:
two serde_json passes per line (the independent count and the decode), the
duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download
pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
the ZSTD level against its 13x CPU cost, parallelize per coin within an
hour), are the open deviation in docs/issues/006-hl-l2book-realdata.md.

duplicate digest, the spill serialize, and the input sha256. Four DuckDB
threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs
times four threads versus 14.1 at twelve jobs times one). On an idle archive
box, twelve to sixteen workers at one thread each should hold the download

threads per worker oversubscribe past eight jobs (4.6 MB/s at sixteen jobs

pace; the levers to get there, in order (drop the double parse, re-measure
